claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an example of a eutectic high-entropy alloy relevant to the hypothesis.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a fine, dual-phase lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure.
The initial fcc/B2 inter-lamellar spacing is approximately 2 μm.
The alloy is initially produced by rapid solidification.
Rapid, short-duration high-temperature annealing immediately after solidification will refine the lamellar spacing.
The annealing treatment will enhance coherent bonding between the fcc and B2 phases.
High-temperature annealing accelerates atomic mobility and thereby permits microstructural reorganization.
Reduced lamellar spacing will increase strength through a Hall–Petch effect.
More coherent fcc/B2 interfaces will improve strain transfer and strain accommodation.
Improved strain transfer and accommodation at fcc/B2 interfaces will enhance ductility.
The annealed alloy will have a statistically significant increase in tensile yield strength relative to the as-cast alloy.
The annealed alloy will have increased or preserved strain-to-failure relative to the as-cast alloy.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 baseline exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off that limits simultaneous property enhancement.
Standard dislocation behavior in the as-cast baseline limits simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement.
The intervention should generalize to eutectic HEAs having similar dual-phase lamellar microstructures.
The intervention may not apply to non-eutectic or markedly compositionally different HEAs.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis promises simultaneous improvements in strength and ductility, whereas the predicted outcome permits ductility merely to be preserved.

Preserved ductility is allowed by the predicted outcome, but the falsification rule requires a statistically significant increase in both strength and ductility; thus an outcome permitted by the prediction would nevertheless falsify the hypothesis.

The intervention is a high-temperature treatment, while the conditions state that it is performed under ambient service conditions. This appears to conflate treatment conditions with subsequent testing or service conditions.
